minutes.headline: Water commissioners moved the master plan presentation to Monday and heard project updates; only minutes were voted.
minutes.summary: The commissioners reviewed the water main replacement (permit and work-hours issues), the pilot studies, SRF funding, ARPA and litigation. The master plan presentation was postponed to a Monday 5 o'clock meeting. They also discussed a second public mailer, paying town employees who help at meetings, and the public bylaw revision.

budget_items.what_was_said: The state permit required removing all AC water main, which the bid did not require; the state engineer replied that pipe off the road and undisturbed can stay. Contract work hours differ from the permit's.

budget_items.topic: SRF funding application for other wells
budget_items.what_was_said: A July submittal for SRF funding is needed for the other wells, and the engineer must prepare it. Funding is competitive, with small systems getting extra points.
The board discussed sending monthly invoices or a lump sum to support ARPA reimbursement for engineering services.
Defendants were found liable, but dollar amounts are not yet known.
ARPA funds approved by the selectmen are paying for the public education effort, master plan and pilot study.

budget_items.topic: Pay for town employees helping at meetings
budget_items.what_was_said: The board supports checking what the town employees are paid for elections so the district compensates them equally.
A second mailer about the special meeting is not in the budget; the consultant's estimate was given, with the actual cost to follow.

decisions.decision: Master plan presentation moved to a meeting on Monday at five o'clock.
Contractor will make an official request to work 7:30 to 3:30 under the permit; the state indicated it would likely change it.
Superintendent to look into what the town pays its employees for elections and meetings so the district can compensate them equally.
Board will send comments on the bylaw back to the public petitioners and possibly hold a quick workshop, but will not revise a public-submitted bylaw without their willingness.
Second mailer to be considered after the first mailer and outreach results; the board is not opposed.
Annual meeting is Saturday March 30, voting 8 to 10, meeting at 10.

what_happened.line: The Water District commissioners moved the master plan presentation to a special meeting on Monday at five o'clock.
The state permit for the water main replacement required removing all asbestos-cement main, which the bid did not; the contractor will formally request work hours of 7:30 to 3:30.
The board said a second public mailer is not in the budget and deferred it until the first mailer's results are known.
The commissioners will send comments on the public-petition bylaw back to its petitioners and will not revise it without their willingness.
The superintendent will look into what the town pays employees who work elections and meetings, so the district can pay its own helpers equally.

why_it_matters: The permit and the bid disagree about how much old pipe must come out, and that gap could change the cost and timing of the water main work on residents' streets.
Public education, the master plan and the pilot study are being paid from ARPA money the selectmen approved, while a second mailer would be an unbudgeted cost.
The annual meeting vote and the public-petition bylaw are matters residents will be asked to decide.
